featured_reviews.name: Aashraya Gattamraju
featured_reviews.review_text:
There are educators who teach concepts. Then there are people who quietly alter your life trajectory without even realising they did.

Dr Aman Bhonsle has been that person for me.

I first learned under him 7 years ago through Transactional Analysis at a point where I was trying to figure out where life was taking me professionally and personally. Confused. Curious. Slightly chaotic. Trying to make sense of myself and the world.

Then came Aman.
AND WHAT AN EXPERIENCE.

I genuinely don't think I have laughed till I cried in classrooms the way I have learning under him.

The man is a RIOT.

Psychologically brilliant. Ridiculously well-read. Sharp. Hilarious. Deeply human. Pop-culturally dangerous in the best way possible because somehow he'll explain a concept using something absurdly relevant and suddenly your brain decides to store it forever.

His examples live in my head RENT FREE years later.
And you don't even realise you're learning because you're too busy laughing.

Then halfway through the lecture he casually says one line that sends you into a full blown existential crisis. And that's his superpower, because you leave feeling lighter, smarter, stronger and more aware.
Like life is manageable and not so hard to face again.
Fast forward 7 years.
I'm almost 30 now. Married. A psychotherapist myself. Still learning. Still terrified by certain life chapters. Still trying to become a better human.

And somehow Aman enters this chapter too through Parenting Coaching.
Now see, some people give information.
Some people give perspective.
Very few give people confidence in themselves.
But he does so effortlessly.
But what stays with me isn't just what he teaches.
It's who he is.
The consistency. The care. The investment. The meticulously detailed material, the depth of dedication. The remembering people years later. The rooting for people. The wanting people to do well in life.
I've done enough trainings and courses over the years to know this isn't common.
People remember what you teach, sure, maybe.
People never forget how you made them feel.
Years later, I still remember both.
That says everything.
Aman you, my friend are a ROCKSTAR!

Trauma can be anything from a single, overwhelming event to a long-term experience of emotional abandonment or abuse. These experiences leave a lasting mark on your mind and body. When trauma occurs, your nervous system goes into overdrive, flooding your body with stress hormones that prepare you to fight, run away, or freeze in the face of a threat. These are the natural survival responses. 

The problem arises when the trauma remains unhealed. Stuck in this heightened state, your nervous system can become overly sensitive, leaving you feeling constantly on edge and anxious. This is why even seemingly small things can trigger overwhelming anxiety – your body is still reacting as if you’re facing a major threat.

How To Spot The Signs of Depression In Teens?

The signs of depression in teens can be tricky to spot. We often think of it as constant sadness and tears, but it can also show up as irritability, disinterest, and isolation. You’re not alone if you’re having trouble seeing the signs. This article can help you navigate these confusing changes and get the support your teen might need.
